chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about men and women, how is the prayer offered over them? He said, 'The man is in front of the women, facing the Imam; they line up one behind the other.'
ai.seo_question: How should men and women be arranged during the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the spatial hierarchy in funeral prayers, establishing that men stand in the front rows while women follow directly behind them, a configuration distinct from the Imam-led congregational prayer structure. This arrangement reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on modesty and order, ensuring that the male mourners lead the supplication while the female mourners remain in a structured, rearward position. The hadith underscores the practical application of gender segregation in ritual worship within the early Shia scholarly tradition.
